heroes.role: Long range damage. Fragile, so she needs healing or protection on a long walk.
heroes.split: Guides split by plan. Unicorn suits a long walk or Queen Charge, and Frosty suits fighting inside the base behind tanks. Some use Sneezy, though it can expose her to Air Defenses.

picks.why: Heals her through a long Queen Charge.
Slows the defences shooting at her.
Breaks walls that block her. On a Queen Walk it can pull her Healers towards itself.
Brings her back invulnerable for a few seconds to finish a target, then she falls.

avoid.why: She outranges it, so it runs ahead of her and gets shot.

heroes.role: Support. With the Eternal Tome his ability protects the army from big hits. He walks or flies over walls.
heroes.split: Sneezy leads at TH17 and up. Some guides still prefer Electro Owl in air mode and Poison Lizard in ground mode.

picks.why: Boogers soak up hits meant for him. Some guides use it only in air mode, while others walk him with it.
Long range suits air mode. The usual pick below TH17.
The usual pick for ground mode. Its poison hits enemy troops and heroes, not defences.
Strong for Warden Walks and Fireball.
Stays protected behind the troops.

avoid.why: He stays behind the troops, so its revive is mostly wasted, unless he leads a Warden Walk.
He outranges it, so it runs ahead of him and gets shot.

heroes.role: Dives over walls and hits defences alone, so staying alive decides how far she gets.
heroes.split: The most disputed hero. Guides variously back Diggy, Spirit Fox, Phoenix and L.A.S.S.I as her best pet.

picks.why: Invisibility lets her dive defences and reset Infernos.
She goes deep alone, so a few invulnerable seconds can finish one more defence.
Stuns the defences she goes for.
A strong combination: it can get ahead of her and tank.
Healing, before the better pets unlock.

avoid.why: She already goes for defences, so it adds nothing.
It leads her into Air Defenses.

heroes.role: Tanky flying hero. He gets stronger when separated from friendly flying units.
heroes.split: Angry Jelly leads for clearing defences. Some Duke Charge armies use Spirit Fox.

picks.why: Keeps him attacking defences.
Invisibility on a Duke Charge.
A few invulnerable seconds to finish a target, then he falls.
Hangs back, so defences rarely target it.

avoid.why: Most ground pets trail a flying hero, and the same goes for Unicorn and Frosty.

heroes.role: Tough melee tank. Good for taking down a corner and making a funnel.
heroes.split: Most guides favour Frosty or Phoenix. Some pick Spirit Fox first instead.

picks.why: Slows the defences wearing him down.
A few invulnerable seconds to finish what he is hitting, then he falls.
Invisibility through the first ring of defences. Poor if he is meant to tank for others.
Clears defences early on.
Opens walls and compartments up close.

avoid.why: His short range leaves it exposed to Air Defenses.
It gets exposed to Air Defenses.

heroes.role: Flying damage dealer that can stay with an air army.
heroes.split: Guides split between Angry Jelly and Electro Owl.

picks.why: Lets him charge with an air army and clear defences.
A few invulnerable seconds to finish off a last defence, then he falls.
Matches his ranged attack. The pick before Angry Jelly unlocks.
Stuns defences while it digs.

avoid.why: Close range, and a poor fit for a flying hero.

pets.L.A.S.S.I: Fast wall-jumper, best on the Royal Champion, who is quick enough to back it up. On the King it dies alone.
pets.Electro Owl: Long range support. The early favourite for the Warden.
pets.Mighty Yak: Opens compartments for a King going in close.
pets.Unicorn: Healing. The classic Queen Charge partner.
pets.Frosty: Slows defences. A popular all-round war pet.
pets.Diggy: Burrows under walls and stuns the target it surfaces beside. Strongest with the Royal Champion.
pets.Poison Lizard: Fast, and poisons enemy heroes and troops. Suits a ground mode Warden.
pets.Phoenix: Brings a fallen hero back for a few invulnerable seconds, then they fall. Best on heroes that dive alone.
pets.Spirit Fox: Invisibility on a hero that needs to get deep.
pets.Angry Jelly: Turns the hero onto defences. Top pick for Dragon Duke and Minion Prince.
pets.Sneezy: Boogers take hits for the hero. Best on a Warden in air mode. Avoid on the King, Queen and Dragon Duke.
pets.Greedy Raven: A farming pet that hits resource buildings. Swap it out for war, unless your plan needs its storage damage.

townHalls.summary: Tanks in front, damage behind, and your first Wall Breakers.

strategies.name: Giants and Archers
strategies.about: Giants soak up the hits while Archers do the damage. Wall Breakers open a way in.
steps: Lure the Clan Castle troops with the Barbarian, and kill them with a few Archers.
Send Giants first, at the defences.
Use Wall Breakers to reach the Mortar early.
Spread Archers behind the Giants, and use the last ones to clean up.

townHalls.summary: Your first hero arrives, and Balloons are strong while anti-air is thin.

strategies.name: Balloons and Archers
strategies.about: Balloons go straight for defences, and most bases here have little to stop them. The King keeps the rest busy.
steps: Lure the Clan Castle troops with the Barbarian, and kill them with the King and a few Archers.
Send the King at the side nearest the Air Defense, to draw fire.
Drop the Balloons together close to the Air Defense, as they hit the nearest defence first.
Once it falls, send the last Balloons at Archer Towers. Finish with Archers.

townHalls.summary: Mix ground and air, and start using spells.

strategies.name: Giants, Wizards and Balloons
strategies.about: A ground push takes out the Air Defense, then Balloons finish from the other side.
steps: Lure the Clan Castle troops with the Barbarian, and kill them with Wizards.
Push the King, Giants and Wizards towards the Air Defense. Break walls with Wall Breakers.
Use Lightning on Clan Castle troops, or to finish a damaged Air Defense. It won't kill a healthy one.
Send Balloons from the opposite side once it falls, then clean up with Archers.

townHalls.summary: Air gets harder with more Air Defenses and the Air Sweeper, so go by ground.

strategies.name: Giant and Wizard push
strategies.about: A full ground push with Healing Spells. Air attacks are inconsistent at this level.
steps: Lure the Clan Castle troops, and kill them with Archers and Wizards behind a Giant.
Lead with the King and Giants, towards Mortars and Wizard Towers.
Follow with Wizards and open walls with Wall Breakers.
Drop Healing Spells a little ahead of the push, so it walks into them.
Clean up with Archers, Barbarians and Balloons.

townHalls.summary: Dragons arrive, and they are the safest three-star for several Town Halls.

strategies.name: Mass Dragons
strategies.about: The most forgiving war army here. It suits Air Defenses near the edges, and struggles when they sit central under Wizard Towers.
steps: Killing one Air Defense takes almost all your spell space here. So this army brings Lightning and no Rage.
Lightning the Air Defense nearest your entry.
Clear one side with the King and Clan Castle troops, to make a funnel.
Spread the Dragons in a line along a flat side, behind the Air Sweeper, with Balloons just behind them.

strategies.name: Mass Hog Riders
strategies.about: A ground option that jumps walls. Traps matter more than with Dragons.
steps: Pull out Clan Castle troops, and kill them with the King and Wizards.
Use the King and the other Wizards to clear one side, so the Hogs don't scatter.
Send Hog Riders together.
Heal a little ahead of them, where splash hits or two Giant Bombs could sit.

townHalls.summary: The Queen arrives, but you still bring only one hero. Learn ground timing with GoHo, or stay on Dragons.

strategies.name: Mass Dragons
strategies.about: Still a strong beginner army here. It struggles when Air Defenses sit central under Wizard Towers.
steps: Earthquake one Air Defense, then Lightning it. Low-level spells may fall short, so count before you cast.
Clear one side with the King, to make a funnel.
Spread the Dragons in a line behind the Air Sweeper, with Balloons just behind them.
Rage them when they reach the core.

strategies.name: GoHo
strategies.about: A Golem and Wizards open the base, the Queen and Valkyries take the core, and Hog Riders clear the rest. Teaches timing and spell placement.
steps: Lure the Clan Castle troops with the Barbarian, and Poison them.
The Golem tanks one side while Wizards clear a funnel.
Send the Queen and Valkyries into the core through a Wall Breaker gap.
Send Hog Riders round the outside to clear defences. Heal ahead of them where defences overlap.

strategies.name: Golem and Valkyrie push
strategies.about: A simple ground push, and a common choice at this level.
steps: Send the Golems first with the King, to take the fire.
Wizards clear the edge buildings, so Valkyries don't wander off course.
Open the first compartment with Wall Breakers.
Send Valkyries through the gap. Poison Clan Castle troops, and heal ahead of the Valkyries.

townHalls.summary: Witches reward steady pressure, and Lava Hounds open up air.

strategies.name: Witch Slap
strategies.about: Golems in front and Witches behind. It wins by pressure more than precision.
steps: Golems first, to take the fire. Enter away from a corner.
Use the King and Queen on each side to funnel. Open the way in with Wall Breakers or Jump.
Deploy Witches behind them, most of them in the centre. Watch for Wizard Towers.
Freeze what locks on, heal ahead of them, and Rage at the core.

strategies.name: Zap Dragons
strategies.about: Spells clear two Air Defenses, then the Dragons have an easy run.
steps: Pick a base with two Air Defenses inside one Earthquake. Earthquake them, then finish both with Lightning.
If they are apart, change your spells or your target.
Use heroes on the remaining Air Defenses, and watch the defending Queen, the main threat to Dragons.
Deploy the Dragons from the side away from the Air Sweeper. Save Balloons and Rage for later in the attack.

strategies.name: Zap Lalo
strategies.about: Lava Hounds tank for Balloons. Strong, but needs precise timing.
steps: Zap the defending Queen if she guards your path. If not, zap an Air Defense. Lure the Clan Castle with Balloons.
Send the King at an Air Defense and the Queen at other big defences.
Lava Hounds first, Balloons close behind, with Haste and Heal on the way in.
Clean up with Minions, the Wizard and the Giant.

townHalls.summary: Inferno Towers arrive. Zap Dragons stays simple, and Queen Charge starts here.

strategies.name: Zap Dragons
strategies.about: Remove Air Defenses before the Dragons deploy. Low risk.
steps: Earthquake and Lightning two Air Defenses that sit close together.
Use the Queen and Prince on what remains.
Deploy the Dragons, with Balloons on the defences in their way.
Rage at the core, and Freeze what locks on.

strategies.name: Queen Charge Hybrid
strategies.about: The Queen with Healers clears one side, then Hog Riders and Miners finish. It struggles against central splash cores, long segmented walls and trap rings.
steps: Open a compartment with Wall Breakers. Walk the Queen in with her Healers, clear of single-target Inferno Towers.
Heal under the Queen as she crosses Inferno Towers. Later Heals go under the swarm, following the damage.
The King cuts the other side.
When splash defences on the path are gone, send Hogs and Miners on a wide arc. Keep a few for clean-up.

strategies.name: Zap Lalo
strategies.about: A classic air three-star for players who already know their timing.
steps: Zap the defending Queen with Lightning, or an Air Defense if she is out of the way.
The Golem tanks for your Queen, and Wall Breakers let her in. The King funnels and draws out the Clan Castle.
Send Lava Hounds first, then Balloons behind them, with Haste and Heal.
Freeze what locks on, and clean up with Minions.

townHalls.summary: Zap Witches is the easy three-star. The Warden and Eagle Artillery change planning.

strategies.name: Zap Witches
strategies.about: Very forgiving. Spells take out the Inferno Towers, then Witches walk through.
steps: Lightning and Earthquake the Inferno Towers.
Send a Golem and some Witches on each flank, to make a wide funnel. Poison Clan Castle troops.
Send the other Witches and heroes through the centre, with Super Wall Breakers opening the core.
Use the Warden's ability in the core, when the push takes heavy damage.

strategies.name: Electro Dragons
strategies.about: One of the easier air armies. Chain lightning needs buildings close together, so it suits compact bases.
steps: Funnel with heroes or one Electro Dragon.
Send the rest in a straight line from the weakest air side, with Balloons behind them.
Rage in the core. Freeze Inferno Towers, Air Defenses or Air Sweepers when the army reaches them.
Poison Clan Castle troops, and clean up with the Baby Dragon.

strategies.name: Queen Charge Hybrid
strategies.about: The versatile option for skilled players. Higher reward, less forgiving.
steps: Queen and Healers clear one side, aiming for the Eagle Artillery, enemy heroes and Clan Castle troops.
The King cuts the opposite side. Heal the Queen as she crosses Inferno Towers.
Send Hog Riders and Miners together between the two funnels. Use Super Wall Breakers to get them in.
Use the Warden's ability as they move through the core.

townHalls.summary: Siege machines arrive and make air attacks more controlled.

strategies.name: Zap Dragons
strategies.about: Simple and reliable, and it doesn't need epic equipment.
steps: Use Giant Arrow on an Air Defense. Lightning and Earthquake two more, or a multi-target Inferno Tower.
Funnel with the King or a Baby Dragon.
Deploy the Dragons in a tight group with Balloons, and the Battle Blimp behind them. Use the Warden's ability early.
Save Rage and Freeze for the Town Hall area.

strategies.name: Yeti Smash
strategies.about: A ground alternative. Yetis and their Yetimites overwhelm the defences behind a tank.
steps: Make a funnel with heroes.
Send the Yetis behind an Ice Golem, which takes the hits.
Freeze what locks on as they reach the core, and Rage them through it.
Clean up with Wizards.

strategies.name: DragBat
strategies.about: Dragons weaken the splash defences, then Bat Spells swarm what's left. Timing decides it.
steps: Deploy Dragons with a Battle Blimp, and Rage them through the core.
Wait until splash defences are weak or gone.
Drop Bat Spells from outside the base, on what is left. Freeze what still threatens the Bats.

strategies.name: Queen Charge Hybrid
strategies.about: Still strong here if you can control the charge.
steps: Queen and Healers clear one side, going for Eagle Artillery and Clan Castle troops.
The King cuts the other side. Heal her through heavy damage.
Send Hog Riders and Miners in a line between the two funnels. Wizards and the rest clean up.
Use the Warden's ability in the core, and Freeze what locks on.

townHalls.summary: The Royal Champion arrives, and Yetis are the ground answer.

strategies.name: Yeti Super Archer Spam
strategies.about: Simple to deploy, with a lot of forgiving damage.
steps: Ice Golems go first, to tank for the push.
Send Yetis in a wide line behind them, with heroes and the Log Launcher through the centre.
Send Super Archers on the flanks, with one in the middle. Use the Warden's ability early.
Rage the heavy areas, and Jump into the core. Poison Clan Castle troops.

strategies.name: Yeti and Super Wizard Smash
strategies.about: A heavy ground push. Keep the heroes grouped under the Warden's ability.
steps: Open a side with heroes and a Log Launcher.
Send Yetis, then Super Wizards through the centre.
Use the Warden's Eternal Tome when the group is under fire, and Freeze what locks on.
The Royal Champion clears side defences, then Bat Spells clean up.

strategies.name: Super Archer Clone Hydra
strategies.about: One of the most reliable air attacks, but with several moving parts. Ask your clan for Super Archers.
steps: Send a Lava Hound with the Battle Blimp towards the core, with Super Archers from your Clan Castle inside.
Where the Super Archers land, cast Invisibility, then Clone, then Rage.
Deploy Dragons, Balloons and Dragon Riders in a line behind the push, with the Warden.
Send the Royal Champion at the back of the base.

townHalls.summary: The Pet House opens. Most guides pick a Dragon army here.

strategies.name: Super Dragons
strategies.about: One of the most reliable armies here, and forgiving to deploy.
steps: Use the Queen on one side and a Baby Dragon on the other, to make a funnel.
Giant Arrow takes out an Air Defense as she goes.
Deploy Super Dragons in a line with Balloons in front, and the Warden and Prince with them.
Rage early, and Freeze Scattershots or Inferno Towers.

strategies.name: Mass Dragons with Blimp
strategies.about: The Queen's Giant Arrow handles an Air Defense, and the Blimp goes for the Town Hall.
steps: Giant Arrow on an Air Defense.
The King makes the path, then Dragons and Balloons go through the middle.
Send the Blimp at the Town Hall with the Warden.
Freeze and Rage where the damage is highest.

strategies.name: RC Walk Dragons
strategies.about: Very strong once the Champion's walk has cleared key defences.
steps: Walk the Royal Champion from a corner. Fire Rocket Spear early, and chain Invisibility to keep her alive.
Use Rocket Balloons on outside defences to guide her. Aim her at the Town Hall or Scattershots.
The King and a Siege Barracks take one side, and the Queen the other.
Deploy the Dragons with the Warden, and use his ability when they reach heavy damage.

townHalls.summary: Root Riders and Dragon Duke arrive, and ground smash takes over.

strategies.name: Root Rider with RC Charge
strategies.about: One of the most consistent high Town Hall ground armies of 2026. Avoid maze bases with many compartments, which scatter its pathing.
steps: Pick your entry by where the Town Hall and Eagle sit. Charge the Royal Champion on that side, to remove a Spell Tower.
Cover her with Invisibility, and Recall her when she has done her job. Use Giant Arrow across the base.
Rocket Balloons hit outside defences, and Super Barbarians clear the edges.
Send Root Riders, Valkyries and Healers at key compartments once the path is set.
Overgrowth pushes them towards the core. Fire the Champion's ability just before it ends.

strategies.name: Warden Charge Super Yetis
strategies.about: The Warden leads with Healers, and Super Yetis push behind him.
steps: Open with the Warden, Healers and Furnaces, to make the funnel and remove a single-target Inferno Tower.
If you can't reach one, let Skeleton Spells tank it. King and Queen cut the other side.
Send Super Yetis through the middle, and Jump into the Town Hall compartment.
Use the Champion at the back of the base.

strategies.name: Hydra
strategies.about: A triple air mix where pathing decides everything. Avoid the Clan Castle.
steps: Plan a path round the Clan Castle, then use the King and Queen to shape the funnel.
Deploy Dragons, Dragon Riders and Balloons through the core.
Send the Battle Blimp at the Town Hall, and drop Clone Spells where it releases its troops.
Freeze and Rage what locks on to the army.

townHalls.summary: Merged defences arrive. Super Yetis and Root Riders lead.
townHalls.note: Picked before Town Hall 19, which Supercell says lands in mid-November 2026. Expect these to change.

strategies.name: Fireball Super Yeti
strategies.about: Safe and consistent on compact bases with stacked defences, but it needs a high-level Fireball. If yours is low, pick another plan.
steps: Walk the Warden to stacked defences. Invisibility on nearer ones locks the Fireball target, and Earthquake finishes it.
Funnel with the Queen on one side and the Baby Dragon on the other.
Send the Ice Golem, Super Yetis, Healers and King into the gap, with Wall Breakers early.
Jump to get the push into the core, and Rage in the heaviest damage.
Send the Royal Champion once the army reaches the middle. Balloons and Minions clean up.

strategies.name: RC Walk Root Riders
strategies.about: Strong, but needs precise control of the Champion's walk.
steps: Walk the Royal Champion with Invisibility, to remove key defences.
Recall her when your Invisibility runs out.
Send Root Riders and Valkyries down a narrow path to the core, with Healers, the Warden and the recalled Champion.
Rocket Balloons and Super Barbarians clear the outside.
Stack Overgrowth on the Town Hall. Use Totems from your Clan Castle where pressure is heaviest.

strategies.name: Root Riders and Valkyries
strategies.about: Controlled ground movement rather than spam.
steps: The King cuts one side, and a Siege Barracks and the Queen cut the other.
Send Root Riders first, then Valkyries once the walls open. Super Barbarians and Healers follow.
Overgrowth narrows the path, and Rage carries them through the heavy damage.
Freeze what locks on, and use the Warden's ability in the core.

strategies.name: RC Walk Dragons
strategies.about: Fast and explosive when the walk takes out the right targets.
steps: Walk the Royal Champion inwards, not along the edge. Cast Invisibility to cover the gaps in the Spirit Fox's.
At the big defences, cast Earthquake and fire her ability. Keep covering her with Invisibility.
The Queen and Ice Golem take the other side, and Giant Arrow hits an Air Defense.
Send Dragons with the Warden, saving his ability for the Town Hall section.
Send Rocket Balloons at outside defences, and clean up with the rest.

townHalls.summary: Sneezy, Meteor Golem and the Firespitter. Check each Firespitter's cone before you pick your entry.
townHalls.note: Picked before Town Hall 19, which Supercell says lands in mid-November 2026. Expect these to change.

strategies.name: Fireball Super Yetis
strategies.about: One of the most consistent smash attacks here, on compact bases. It needs a high-level Fireball.
steps: Walk the Warden to stacked defences. Invisibility locks the Fireball target, and Earthquake finishes it.
The Queen and a Baby Dragon make the funnel.
Ice Golems go in first to take the hits, then Super Yetis, Healers and the King.
Jump from your Clan Castle leads them into the core. Rage in the heaviest damage.
Send the Royal Champion at the centre, and Skeleton the Monolith.

strategies.name: RC Walk Dragons
strategies.about: Extremely strong when the walk works. Invisibility is used on the spot to steer the Dragons' path.
steps: Walk the Royal Champion from a corner with Invisibility.
Rocket Balloons help steer her path.
When the walk ends, the Queen's Giant Arrow and a Siege Barracks take the other side and its Air Defenses.
Deploy Dragons with the Warden and Prince on the opposite side, using Invisibility to steer them.

strategies.name: RC Walk Root Riders
strategies.about: One of the strongest ground strategies here.
steps: Walk the Royal Champion with Invisibility, to remove key defences and make a funnel.
Recall the Champion once she has done her job.
Send Root Riders, Valkyries and Healers with the Warden, the Champion and a Troop Launcher.
Wall Breakers open the first compartment. Rocket Balloons, Super Barbarians and Archers clear the outside.
Overgrowth on the Town Hall area, and Freeze what locks on.

strategies.name: Hydra Air
strategies.about: A two-flank air attack that needs Air Defenses you can split. Avoid it when they sit central under Wizard Towers.
steps: Check the Air Defenses can be split into two flanks.
Open with a Lava Hound and Balloons.
Send Dragons and Dragon Riders from both flanks.
Rage them through the core, Freeze what locks on, and Poison Clan Castle troops.

townHalls.summary: Supercell's July war data had Dragon armies and Throwers with Healers at about 40% of TH18 attacks. Both were cut afterwards.
townHalls.note: Picked before Town Hall 19, which Supercell says lands in mid-November 2026. Expect these to change.

strategies.name: Super Yeti with RC Charge
strategies.about: The most forgiving three-star at this Town Hall.
steps: Soften a cluster of key defences with Fireball or a Log Launcher.
Send an Ice Golem as the tank, then charge the Royal Champion with Electro Boots.
Drop the Super Yetis behind her charge, with Healers and the Super Wall Breakers.
Rage them through the core. Freeze the Guardian, as it won't wake while Frozen. Balloons and Minions clean up.

strategies.name: Root Rider Yeti
strategies.about: Root Riders push defences and Super Yetis push the core. Avoid tight compartment bases, which scatter ground pathing.
steps: The King and Queen make the funnel.
Charge the Royal Champion through it with Electro Boots, to tank.
Send Root Riders at key defences. An Ice Golem and Super Yetis take the core, with Healers behind.
Skeleton the Monolith. Freeze the Guardian, and Rage through the core. Balloons and Archers clean up.

strategies.name: Dragon Duke Charge Hydra
strategies.about: From the most used army type in Supercell's July data. Dragon Riders and the Duke were cut in July, and Fire Heart in October. Older hit rates may flatter it.
steps: Start the Duke from a corner, clear of Seeking Air Mines. Keep other air troops away from him.
Cast Invisibility about every 10 seconds while the Spirit Fox lives, then about every 4.
When the Duke falls, send the Queen to the opposite corner, then the Lava Hound first.
Riders, Inferno Dragons, Warden and Prince follow. Totem the Guardian, defending heroes and big defences.
Revive the Duke from your Clan Castle once the army reaches him. Send Rocket Balloons at outside defences.

strategies.name: Rocket Backpack Throwers
strategies.about: Second most used army type in Supercell's July data, before Throwers lost health, damage and speed in September. Best on bases with one tight group of defences.
steps: Ask your clan for Earthquakes. Send the Duke at a tight group, then cast one and fire his Rocket Backpack beside it.
Cast your other Earthquake and all your Lightning on the next line of defences. These must hit the right group.
Ice Golem, then Throwers and Healers from a corner. The Champion widens the funnel, and the Queen opens a second.
A Super Wall Breaker opens the first compartment. Overgrowth keeps the Throwers grouped, and Super Barbarians clear the outside.
Use Totems early, on the Guardian and defending heroes. Freeze the worst damage, and watch the clock.

strategies.name: Duke Charge Super Bowlers
strategies.about: A hard-hitting ground push for compact bases and bases built to stop air.
steps: Start the Duke from a corner. Cast Invisibility about every 10 seconds while the Spirit Fox lives, then about every 4.
Let him clear the whole side before you commit the main army.
Send Ice Golems and Super Bowlers with Healers, the Warden and the Sky Wagon. King and Queen take the other side.
Rage with the Warden's ability as they get inside, then Rage again. Freeze the Guardian.
Revive the Duke from your Clan Castle once the army reaches him.

strategies.name: Ruin Witch
strategies.about: Supercell put Ruin Witch attacks at about 76% three-stars, against a 53% average. That was before October's nerf to her Ruin Knights, so it may flatter her. Throwers were also cut in September.
steps: Ask your clan for Earthquakes. Walk the Duke to the defences, then cast one and fire his Rocket Backpack.
Use your other Earthquakes and all your Lightning on what the Backpack weakened.
The Warden and Healers set the funnel. Keep it clean, as Ruin Witches can't jump walls.
Send Throwers and the Queen on one side, and the Champion on the other.
Drop Ruin Witches behind the Throwers, away from defences, so there is rubble for Ruin Knights.
Overgrowth the Monolith and Firespitter section, and Skeleton the Monolith. Totem the Guardian.
Freeze Firespitters or Inferno Towers mid-push, and save one Freeze for a Revenge Tower.

Barbarian.role: Cheap filler for funnels, clean-up and taking the first shots.
use: Drop a few at the edge first to draw fire and set off traps.
Use them to clear outside buildings so stronger troops walk inwards.

use.t: A Mortar cannot hit troops right beside it, so drop Barbarians next to an exposed one.

beware.t: Splash from Mortars and Wizard Towers kills a clump, so spread them out.

beware: Too weak to carry an attack past the low Town Halls.

Archer.role: Cheap ranged damage that shoots over walls.
use: Spread them behind a tank, so defences are shooting something else.
A thin line clears outside buildings quickly.
beware: Very little health. Splash wipes a clump, so never drop them in one spot.

Goblin.role: Farming troop that goes for resources before anything else.
use: Send them once something else is drawing fire near the storages.
Pick them for loot raids, not for stars.
They do double damage to resource buildings, and the Town Hall counts as one.
beware: They ignore the defences shooting them, and have little health.

Giant.role: Low Town Hall tank that walks to the nearest defence.
use: Drop them first, then damage troops once defences have locked on.
Open a wall for them, or they lose time hitting it.

use.t: A Healer behind the group keeps them going, once the Air Defense is down.

beware: Low damage, so they stall without support.

beware.t: Golems take over as the tank. After that, Giants are mainly cheap decoys that draw fire.

Wall Breaker.role: Opens walls, so ground troops reach the defences instead of stalling.
use: Send them just after your tank, while defences are looking elsewhere.
Send small groups, so one trap or Mortar shot does not lose them all.
They run for the nearest walled building, so the drop point picks the wall. Send one first to check.
beware: They die to almost anything, including a Bomb hidden by the wall.
Sent too early, they die before they reach the wall.

Balloon.role: Slow flying bomber that goes for defences and hits hard.

use.t: Send Giants at the Air Defense first, then Balloons once it is down or busy.

use: Send them together from one side, so they arrive as a group.

use.t: Send them behind a Lava Hound, which soaks up the Air Defense fire.
Haste keeps them moving through Air Defense range.

beware: They are slow and cannot hit air troops, so Air Defenses get plenty of time to shoot them.

beware.t: Seeking Air Mines and Scattershots hit them hard too.
Air Sweepers push them back, so come from behind or the side of one.

Wizard.role: Fragile splash damage that hits ground and air.
use: Keep them behind a tank, spread in a line.
Good at clearing groups of buildings and enemy swarms.
beware: Very little health once the tank has gone.

Healer.role: Keeps ground troops and heroes alive. Does no damage.
Healer.targets: Nearest ground troop or hero, to heal it
use: She locks onto the nearest ground troop, so drop her just behind the one you want healed.
Pair with troops that bunch up, such as Giants, as one Healer can then cover several.
Deal with Air Defenses on the route first, or plan a path around them.

use.t: A Queen Walk is the classic use.
A bunched Thrower pack is the other.

beware: Air Defenses kill them, and the army collapses after that.

beware.t: Seeking Air Mines hit them hard too, so check the route.

beware: They cannot heal air units or Siege Machines. Past four or five on one target, extras add little.

Dragon.role: Tough flying splash damage. The main army at TH7, and still used well above it.
use: Remove or weaken Air Defenses first with Lightning.

use.t: A Giant Arrow or a hero walk can also weaken Air Defenses.

use: Make a funnel so they walk into the core, not around the edge.
Save Rage for the core.
beware: Air Defenses plus Seeking Air Mines, especially at higher Town Halls without a Lightning plan.
Without a funnel they drift round the outside and time runs out.

P.E.K.K.A.role: Big melee damage and health in one body.
use: Send behind a Golem with Wizards and Wall Breakers.
It hits the nearest building, so drop it where the toughest buildings are closest.
beware: Single target, so Skeleton Traps and swarms waste its time.

beware.t: Single-target Infernos and the Monolith melt it, so keep a Freeze for them.
Under 3% of TH18 war attacks in Supercell's October figures, before its damage buff.

use: Use them to clean up edges or fill spare housing in an air army.
Seeking Air Mines ignore them, so they will not clear those. One sent ahead can bait Air Bombs.
beware: Very fragile. Air Bombs and Wizard Towers make short work of a group, so keep them spread.

Hog Rider.role: Fast ground troop that jumps walls and goes for defences.
use: Kill the Clan Castle troops first, as Hogs will not fight back. Make a funnel too, or they scatter.
Heal them ahead of where they are going, not where they stand.

use.t: Keep a Freeze for the Inferno Tower that locks on.

beware: Two Giant Bombs together can wipe out a group.

beware.t: Infernos burn the group unless they are Frozen.
Under 3% of TH18 war attacks in Supercell's October figures, before their health buff.

Valkyrie.role: Melee spinner that shreds groups of buildings and troops at once.
use: Best where buildings sit tightly together, usually the core.
Send them behind a tank through an open funnel.
Rage on a group inside the core is the payoff.
beware: Walls cost her a lot of time, so have an entry ready.

Golem.role: The main tank at middle Town Halls. Walks to defences and soaks up fire.
use: Drop first and let defences lock on.

use.t: A Freeze stops an Inferno burning it down and resets the beam.

use: Follow with Wall Breakers, then your damage troops.
Golemites still draw fire after it falls, so give them time to work.
beware: Very little damage, so it needs an army behind it.

beware.t: Ice Golems and Root Riders largely take over its tank job higher up.

Witch.role: Support that keeps raising Skeletons to soak up shots.
use: Keep her behind a tank, and let the Skeletons distract the defences.
They waste single-target shots. Splash clears them fast, so remove Wizard Towers and Bomb Towers early.

use.t: Mass Witches are a common plan at middle Town Halls.

beware: Each Skeleton is weak, so Witch armies win by steady pressure, not by burst damage.
Slow and fragile if the front line falls.

Lava Hound.role: Flying tank that goes for Air Defenses and soaks up their fire.
use: Send it first, from the side of the Air Defense you want to tie up.
Air troops follow once it has taken the Air Defense's attention.
When it dies, the Lava Pups keep drawing fire for a moment.
beware: It does almost no damage, so it needs air troops behind it.

Bowler.role: Ranged ground splash whose boulders bounce into whatever is behind.
use: Send them behind a tank, and let the bounce hit two buildings at once.
The bounce carries on along the same line, so it can hit a defence behind an outer building.
They work well where buildings are packed together.
beware: Slow, and they cannot hit air troops, so enemy air units need another answer.

Baby Dragon.role: Flying splash that gets much stronger when no other air unit is near.
use: Use one or two apart from your air group to clear the outside for a funnel.
Send it where it can work alone, as its bonus needs that.
beware: Nearby air troops switch off its bonus damage and attack speed.
Other Baby Dragons count too, so drop them well apart.

Miner.role: Tunnels under walls, and comes up right beside each target.
use: Walls do not slow them, so they suit heavily walled bases.
Healing Spells and Healers keep the group going when they surface.
They still get spell bonuses underground.
beware: They only take damage and set off traps above ground, and they hit one target at a time.
Giant Bombs beside defences can catch them as they surface.

beware.t: Under 3% of TH18 war attacks in Supercell's October figures, before their health buff.

Yeti.role: Heavy ground hitter, whose Yetimites come out as it takes damage.
use: Make a funnel first, then send them in a group to smash through.

use.t: A Log Launcher ahead of them opens the way.

use: Save Rage for when they reach the core.
beware: Multi-target Infernos cut through the swarm.
Slow, so a late start can run out of time.

Ice Golem.role: Tank that goes for defences, then freezes the area when destroyed.
use: Send one to soak up fire ahead of a push.
Let it die among defences, so the freeze stops them shooting your main group.
Dying beside a single-target Inferno stops it burning your tank for those seconds.
beware: Low damage, so it only sets things up.
A freeze far away from your army helps nobody.

Electro Dragon.role: Slow flying lightning that chains between close buildings.
use: Remove Air Defenses first with Lightning, or send Balloons at them alongside.
A group can clear a compartment quickly when buildings sit close together.
It strikes the ground when destroyed, which can finish off damaged buildings.
beware: Very slow, so a long walk can run out the clock.
Chains do less on spread-out bases.

Dragon Rider.role: Flying heavy hitter that goes straight for defences.
use: Open with a hero or tank so it reaches defences while they are distracted.
Freeze buys time when it gets into the core.

use.t: A Totem Spell also buys time in the core.

beware: Air Defenses and Seeking Air Mines. A few Balloons sent ahead set off the mines.
It leaves other buildings standing, so plan who cleans up.

Headhunter.role: Goes straight for enemy heroes, jumps walls, and slows them with poison.
use: Drop her close to a defending hero, so she gets there quickly.
She dies fast, so send a couple together or shield her with a Giant.
Removing a hero early protects your main push.
beware: Little use once the enemy heroes are gone.
She will not clear a route, as she ignores other targets while a hero is up.

beware.t: Do not count on her to deal with Guardians.

Electro Titan.role: Walking tank with an aura that damages everything around her.
use: She goes for whatever is nearest, so clear the side first or she wanders the edge.
Walk her with the main group, so her aura and health both help.
beware: Short range, so she walks right into defences and takes the hits.
Single-target Infernos burn through her, so Freeze them or give them cheap targets.

Apprentice Warden.role: Ground support whose aura gives nearby troops extra health.
use: Walk him with tough troops, so the aura covers as many as possible.
His aura does not stack with the Grand Warden's, so keep them with different groups.
Drop him behind the front so he reaches the middle of the group.
beware: No Eternal Tome, so he only adds health, not protection from big hits.
Siege Machines get nothing from the aura.

Ruin Witch.role: Support that turns rubble into Ruin Knights. She never attacks.
use: Drop her behind the front line once the first buildings have fallen.
She goes to the closest rubble, however far, so drop her where that leads inward.
A few can support a Thrower push. Armies built around her run about six.

use.t: Top three-star rate in Supercell's October TH18 war figures, taken before the Knights' nerf.

beware: Dropped too early she stands idle, and near defences she dies before making Knights.
She ignores wall rubble and rubble behind walls, so open the compartment first.
Spring Traps can throw Knights since October.

Root Rider.role: Ground bruiser that smashes walls and goes for defences.
use: Send a group to open a walled base for the rest. Full Rider armies run seven to twelve.
Overgrowth stops a cluster of defences firing and Riders walk past them. They wake up undamaged later.
Save Rage for the core. Raged on a wall line, they can cross without breaking it.
Keep a Freeze for the defence melting them.
beware: The Monolith hits high health troops hardest, so Freeze it or give it a Skeleton Spell as they arrive.

Druid.role: Heals several troops at once, then turns into a Bear as a fighter.
Druid.targets: Heals nearby troops. Its Bear goes for defences first
use: Send with heroes on a dive for quick healing.
Works best with a few big targets, such as heroes or Super Witches. Swarms spread its healing thin.
Unlike Healers, Druids heal air troops too, such as Dragons and Electro Dragons.
beware: Bears go for defences but cannot cross walls, so Druids struggle on heavily walled bases.
Healing stops once it turns, so plan the walk around that.

Thrower.role: Long range damage that hits ground and air. Most defences still outrange it.
use: Clear both shoulders first, so they walk into the core. A hero or two Root Riders each side does it.
Keep the pack bunched so Healers can cover it. Four or five Healers is usual.
Freeze the splash defences, and Rage a pack that has stalled.
beware: Without a funnel they wander the edge and shoot storages.
Air Defenses ignore them but kill the Healers, which collapses the attack.
Scattershots and multi-target Infernos punish the bunch. Skeleton Traps soak up spears while defences fire.

Furnace.role: Sits still and sends Firemites at buildings over its lifetime.
Furnace.targets: Stays put. Its Firemites go for buildings
use: Place it out of range of defences, by the outside buildings you want gone.
Use it to clear one side of a funnel, so the rest of the army gets deeper.
beware: Destroyed early, its remaining Firemites are lost.
Hidden Teslas can zap it and cut its Firemites, so drop it farther out than you think.

Meteor Golem.role: Tank that splits into two Meteormites on each throw, then re-forms.
use: Start with a couple up front. Halves merge with any nearby half, and merging gives brief immunity.
Use a hero or side troops to set the entry point.
Pair with Throwers for damage, as it cannot win alone.
Bring something that hits air, such as the Archer Queen, to cover enemy air troops.
beware: Spread too thin, the halves die alone and never re-form.
Only Meteormites cross walls, not a whole Golem. Cloned ones cannot merge.

Super Barbarian.role: Fast funnel maker, useful both in war armies and for farming.
use: Use them to clear the outside and open a funnel for the main army.
Their Rage lasts only the first few seconds, so drop them right next to their targets.
Also good for farming, as they clear collectors on the outside quickly.

beware.t: Few high-end armies use them for much else.

beware: They die quickly to splash when bunched.

Super Archer.role: Arrows pierce through buildings and reach targets several buildings away.

use.t: Drop them in a Battle Blimp from your Clan Castle, with Invisibility, to remove a key defence.

use: Use them to make a funnel or clean up, as they reach so far.

use.t: They spam well alongside Yetis.
Mostly a farming pick by now: a Super Archer Blimp or a mass of them loots quickly.

beware: Invisibility only covers troops inside its ring, so archers that walk out of it get shot.

beware.t: The Eagle Artillery can catch them.
Scattershots can catch them.

Super Wall Breaker.role: Rolling bomb that always blows up, so it gets through where normal ones die. Mainly a war troop.
use: Use for wall spots covered by a multi-target Inferno Tower.
Good for opening a chosen section on a Queen Charge.

use.t: A staple of top war armies, where one or two open each new compartment.

beware: Each one takes much more army space than a plain Wall Breaker, which is often enough for a cheap raid.

Super Giant.role: Very tanky, and punches through walls. A niche pick, rare in war at the top.
use: Use as a tank in a push, with Healers behind.
It heads for defences like a Giant, and breaks any wall in its way much faster.
beware: Slow with low damage, so hard to justify the boost at higher Town Halls.
It can break walls in unhelpful spots.

Wall Wrecker.role: Drives straight at the Town Hall, smashing walls. Your Clan Castle troops drop when it dies or you tap.
use: Use to open the base at a chosen spot for a ground army or Queen Charge.
Put a tank or heroes with it, as it draws heavy fire.
beware: Single-target Infernos melt it.
Not for air armies, as Clan Castle air troops can meet Seeking Air Mines.
It cannot be healed and spells do not affect it, but the Grand Warden's Eternal Tome protects it.

Battle Blimp.role: Flying delivery. It flies straight at the Town Hall, and you tap to drop your Clan Castle troops along that line.
use: Use it to remove a key defence with Clan Castle troops, plus Rage where they land.
Send a Balloon or two ahead, to clear Seeking Air Mines.
Invisibility protects the troops it drops, not the Blimp itself.
beware: Low health, so Air Defenses bring it down quickly if it flies too far.
Little damage of its own.

Sneaky Goblin.role: Goblin that stays hidden for only the first few seconds after deployment. Mainly a farming troop.
use: Drop them close to storages, so the cloak is not wasted on the walk.
Use them for farming, as they strip storages quickly with double damage to resources.

use.t: Pair with a Battle Blimp to take out the Town Hall for a quick star.
A Goblin Blimp is among the fastest farming raids.

beware: Little health once revealed, and not a main war troop.

Super Miner.role: Tunnelling Miner whose damage builds on one target. It drops an exploding barrel when it falls. Mainly for farming.
use: Use it for farming, where a quick Super Miner raid takes loot fast.
Keep Healing Spells and Healers ready when the group surfaces.
beware: Few war armies use it, and it is barely picked in war at the very top.
October's health buff only helps max levels, so test it in a friendly before taking it to war.

Rocket Balloon.role: Balloon with booster rockets that gets to defences quickly. Mainly a war troop.
use: Send them after a Lava Hound or a hero has drawn the first shots.
The speed gets them in before Air Defenses thin them out.

use.t: A few can snipe outside defences, so your Dragons or heroes path inward.

beware: The rockets last only a few seconds, so drop them close to their targets.
Seeking Air Mines still punish them.

beware.t: Scattershots punish them too.

Stone Slammer.role: Flying machine that goes for defences and ignores other targets until they fall. Its splash also breaks nearby walls.
use: Good with defence-targeting troops such as Hogs and Balloons, to clear the outer defences.
Used in LaLoon and Queen Walk setups to open a path.
beware: Tougher than a Blimp, but Air Defenses still bring it down, so send it on their weaker side.
It cannot hit air troops, so check the enemy Clan Castle for them first.

Inferno Dragon.role: Beam that builds up the longer it stays on one target. Mainly a war troop.
use: It hits whatever is closest, so place it where tough buildings come first.

use.t: Used in Duke Charge air armies alongside Dragon Riders.

beware: Poor at clearing lots of small buildings, as the beam starts again on each new target.

Super Valkyrie.role: Spinning splash with a wider reach, leaving Rage when she falls.
use: Send several, so one falling boosts the others.
Suits spam attacks with no room for your own Rage Spells.

use.t: Mostly a Clan Castle pick in top war armies, and rarely the main troop.

beware: In an enemy Clan Castle, her falling Rage boosts defences too, so kill her away from them.
Each one takes a lot of army space, and you have little control over where she goes.

Super Witch.role: Summons one big tanky Big Boy instead of many Skeletons. A steady war pusher, strongest at mid Town Halls.
use: Let the Big Boys tank at the front, with Healers and the Warden behind.
A common plan: a Warden Walk with Fireball opens a section, then they push through.

use.t: Druids keep them alive through the heaviest damage.
Rare at this level, so look at other armies first.

beware: She is slow, so start with plenty of time.

beware.t: Scattershots hit a big group hard, so keep a Freeze for them.
Keep a Freeze for the Monolith too, if she has to pass it.

Siege Barracks.role: Lands, releases P.E.K.K.As and Wizards, and then your Clan Castle troops.
Siege Barracks.targets: Stays where it lands, and does not attack
use: Use it on a flank to help make a funnel, or to clean up when time is short.
Good when you want a distraction, not Clan Castle troops landed deep in the base.
beware: It stays on the outside, and you have little control after that.
It cannot tank, and its health keeps falling.

Ice Hound.role: Tanky flyer that slows what it hits and freezes the area where it comes down.
use: Use like a Lava Hound, tying up Air Defenses for your flyers.
Time your followers so they arrive as the freeze lands.
beware: A niche pick on attack, and better known in a defending Clan Castle. Boost it only when you want its freeze.
Little damage on its own, so it needs air troops behind it.

Super Bowler.role: Slow ground splash with boulders that hit three times. Mainly a war troop.
use: Send a group through a funnel, behind a tank, for big damage on packed buildings.
Save Rage for the core.

use.t: A leading war plan: a hero charge clears one side, then the Bowlers push through.

beware: Slow, so long routes can run out the clock. They also cannot hit air troops.
Skeleton Traps can stall the group, as they stop to deal with the skeletons.

beware.t: Keep a Freeze for the Monolith.

Super Dragon.role: Flying fire that destroys clusters of buildings in bursts. Mainly a war troop.
use: Use a mass of them with a funnel, like Mass Dragons.
Rage and Freeze keep the group alive through the core.

use.t: A forgiving main plan: funnel the sides, then spam them in a line with Balloons in front.

beware.t: Less common as the main plan, though some spam armies still use it at the top.

beware: Each one takes a lot of army space, so a bad funnel costs you dearly.

Super Wizard.role: Magic that chains between targets. Mainly a war troop.
use: Use to make a funnel or clear a section.
Often dropped from a Battle Blimp with Invisibility, which keeps these fragile troops alive.

use.t: Used with Yetis for smash.

beware: Chains best where buildings sit close together.
Fragile, so keep a tank in front.

beware.t: Rare in top war armies, even after January's health buff.

Super Minion.role: Flying troop whose first shots reach very far, before it drops to short range. Mainly war support.
use: Support for air armies. Its long shots run out quickly, and then it has to close in.
Also a strong Clan Castle defender.
beware: Too big to slip past Seeking Air Mines, unlike normal Minions.
Better in small numbers than as the main army.

Log Launcher.role: Rolls logs ahead of it that smash walls for ground armies.
use: It drives at the Town Hall, so place it on the line you want opened, then follow with ground troops.
Put a tank in front to take the fire, so it lasts its full time.
Good against ringed bases, as its logs roll on past the outer walls.
beware: Its health keeps falling and nothing heals it, so its time is short.
Slow, and no use to an air army.

Flame Flinger.role: Lobs fire at defences from very long range.
use: Use it to pick off edge defences from outside their reach, before your main troops go in.
Put a tank in front to take the fire, as nothing can heal it.
beware: Slow, so it can cost you the clock.
X-Bows and Mortars can still reach it, and traps can still catch it.

beware.t: A Monolith can reach it too, so clear that first or stay away from it.

Battle Drill.role: Burrows under walls to the nearest defence, pops up and stuns it, then digs to the next one.
use: Use it to take out a chosen defence, by placing it close to that defence.
Plan the line it takes, as it goes for the nearest one.
Send heroes close behind, so they follow it into the core.
beware: It hits one defence at a time, so check which defence is nearest before you drop it.

beware.t: Rarely picked in top war armies, so other machines may suit your plan better.

Super Hog Rider.role: Hog and Rider who split when defeated. The Hog keeps hunting defences, and the Rider hits the nearest building.
use: Like Hog Riders, they hop walls and head straight for defences.
Keep Healing Spells for the splash areas on their way.

beware.t: Rare in top war armies. October's health buff may help, so test it in a friendly first.

Troop Launcher.role: Stays put, firing barrels of Barbarians, Archers, Giants and Wall Breakers at your army, each with one Clan Castle troop.
use: Its barrels aim at your largest group by housing, so keep the main push together.
Place it out of reach of Mortars, X-Bows and Archer Towers. Barrels reach any distance, only slower.
Suits ground pushes such as Root Riders, Super Yetis and Super Bowlers.
beware: It will not fire for one small troop alone, or for spell Skeletons and Bats.
There are only a few barrels and it has a set lifetime, so do not waste it on a thin attack.
If it falls, the barrels left are lost, but your Clan Castle troops still drop.

Super Yeti.role: Heavy ground hitter that carries the core. When hit it releases small mites that shock nearby buildings. Mainly a war troop.
use: Send with a tank in front, then Rage as the group reaches the core.
Open walls early with Wall Breakers, so they do not wander round the outside.
A forgiving plan with a Royal Champion charge.

use.t: Root Riders open the way and Super Yetis carry the core.

beware: Each one takes a lot of army space, so a bad funnel costs you dearly.

beware.t: The Monolith hits high health troops hardest, so keep a Freeze or Skeleton Spell for it.

Sky Wagon.role: Flying machine that goes for defences and drops barrels of air troops and your Clan Castle troops.
use: Deploy it behind your air troops.
Suits air armies, and ground pushes with Healers, where its Balloons set off Seeking Air Mines.
Still a strong pick after its May cut, sent in with Dragons, Dragon Riders or Super Bowlers.
Barrel troops use the Wagon's level, not your Laboratory's, so upgrading it matters.
beware: If it falls early, the barrels left are lost, but your Clan Castle troops still drop.
Its own attack does almost nothing, so its worth is in the barrels.

Lightning Spell.role: Removes Air Defenses before an air attack.
use: Work out how many it takes to kill an Air Defense: its health divided by your Lightning damage.

use.t: An Earthquake first saves spells on a tough target.

use: Also handy on Clan Castle troops or a lone Wizard Tower.

use.t: One bolt makes a single-target Inferno retarget, which restarts its damage. Handy when that Inferno is nearly dead.

beware: Small radius, so check where your strikes land.
It does no damage to storages, so do not aim at them.

Healing Spell.role: Keeps a push alive through sustained fire, on the ground or in the air.
use: Place it 3 to 4 tiles ahead of the group, so they walk into it.
Best for groups, such as Giants, Hog Riders or Miners, as every troop inside gets the full heal.
Wait until the group is around half health, or a splash defence or Giant Bomb has just hit them.
beware: Dropped where troops stand now, they walk straight out of it.
Heroes heal at a lower rate than troops, as the chart shows.

Rage Spell.role: The damage and speed boost that finishes off the core.
use: Drop it 3 to 4 tiles ahead as the main push nears the core, so they walk into it.
Save it for a group that is starting to stall.
beware: Wasted at the start of an attack, or on troops already winning.
Heroes get half the boost and Siege Machines none. A second Rage on the same spot adds nothing.

Jump Spell.role: Lets ground troops walk over a section of wall.
use: Place it where the whole group needs to enter the compartment.
Lets you bring fewer Wall Breakers.
Best over two or three wall layers. On a single wall, Wall Breakers do the job for less.
beware: Troops will only use it if their route takes them there, so check your funnel.
Hog Riders, air troops and wall-hopping heroes gain nothing from it.

Freeze Spell.role: Stops defences and Clan Castle troops inside it for a few seconds.
use: Cast it the moment a defence locks on to your key unit, not before.

use.t: Priorities: Inferno on a hero, Scattershot on a cluster, Spell Tower on the army.
Freezing a single-target Inferno also resets its damage to the lowest stage.
Freeze the Eagle Artillery just before a volley.

beware: Aim to catch two defences if they sit close. Anything outside the circle keeps fighting.
A second Freeze on the same defence at the same time adds nothing, so use it elsewhere.

Poison Spell.role: Kills or slows Clan Castle troops. Does nothing to buildings.
use: Lure the Clan Castle, then Poison them once they are fighting your bait, so they stay in the cloud.
They also attack and move slower, so it buys time.
beware: Do not send the Queen at Valkyries or Super Valkyries with no Poison on them. It wastes her ability and Healers.
On defending heroes it is mainly a slow, as they resist its damage.

Earthquake Spell.role: Opens walls and softens tough buildings by a share of their health.
use: Four open a compartment by breaking any wall of any level. Fewer only weaken it.
One before Lightning cracks a defence, as it takes a share of the defence's health first.

use.t: Soften high-health buildings, such as Eagle Artillery and Infernos, before troops arrive.

beware: Each repeat on the same spot does less.
It hits buildings and walls, not storages or air units.

beware.t: Level 6 and up also hurts defending ground troops.

Haste Spell.role: Faster movement with no damage boost, for one housing space.
use: Cast it on Balloons as they push past mid-base, to stop them stalling under Air Defenses.
Use it when troops must get moving again, as with flyers pushed back by an Air Sweeper.
beware: No damage boost, so Rage is better once troops are hitting the core.
A second Haste adds nothing, and do not count on it adding to Rage's speed.

Clone Spell.role: Makes temporary copies of troops that enter it.
use: Cast it on your mid-base Dragons, or on the troops about to enter the core.
Send the troop you want copied in first, so it reaches the ring ahead of the rest.
beware: There is a housing limit, so it clones only so many at once. Clones also last a short time.
A troop too big for one spell's limit cannot be copied, so check its housing against your level.
Aim it at troops, as heroes cannot be cloned.

Skeleton Spell.role: Instant distraction anywhere on the map, and does not set off traps.
use: Use it on a single-target defence to waste its shots.

use.t: It is cheap cover against the Monolith.

beware: Do not count on Skeletons to finish a Town Hall. Use them to distract.
Skeletons can wander, so results vary.

Bat Spell.role: A swarm of Bats that flies straight at defences, and does not set off traps.
use: Aim at defences that cannot hit air, such as Mortars. Clear or Freeze Wizard Towers first.
Drop it once your Dragons or Yetis have cleared the splash defences, or Bats die quickly.
Give them a tank such as a Lava Hound, but keep them apart, as an Air Bomb on the tank can wipe them.
beware: Do not count on Bats to finish a Town Hall. Aim them at defences.
Bats die quickly to splash and multi-target defences.

Invisibility Spell.role: Hides your units and enemy buildings inside it, except walls and Siege Machines. Troops drop a hidden target.
use: Cast it on a hero as an Inferno starts to burn, or across the route of a charge.
Cast over buildings, it steers troops past them, as they skip what they cannot see.

use.t: Use it on Clan Castle troops after a Blimp drop, so they reach their target.

beware: Over a building your troops are hitting, they drop it and walk on, so aim with care.
It works only inside the circle. A unit that walks out is visible again almost at once.

beware.t: It does not hide your Blimp or other Siege Machines.

Recall Spell.role: Sends troops, heroes and pets back to your deployment bar, to use again elsewhere.
use: Pull a hero walk out while it still has health, then start a second funnel on another side.
Use it to rescue a push that has gone the wrong way, or to save units from a lethal defence.
Redeploy where your Jump or Healing Spells can help.
beware: It does not heal. It takes heroes first, then the biggest units, so a crowd can leave Healers or the pet behind.
Anything left undeployed at the end is lost, and Siege Machines cannot be recalled.

beware.t: Totems cannot be recalled.

Overgrowth Spell.role: Roots buildings: they stop firing, cannot be hit, and your troops ignore them.
use: Drop it on the defensive core, ahead of the push and in the direction of travel.
Centre it on a gap between buildings, to catch more defences.
Ground armies gain most. Electro Dragons gain least, as their chains waste on rooted buildings.

use.t: Root Riders are the classic partner.

beware: Do not root the building your army is hitting, or the whole pack reroutes.
Walls, traps, Clan Castle troops and heroes still work inside it. Your troops can still be shot from outside it.
Weak on spread-out bases. A hero inside it finds nothing to hit, though rooting a side can funnel a Queen past it.

Revive Spell.role: Brings back a fallen hero with most of their health. Select it and tap the hero's pulsing icon, not the ground.
use: Bring it when a hero has to survive deep in the base, where its job is not done.
Wait until the area around the fallen hero is safer, or they will fall again straight away.
beware: Casting it the moment a hero falls is the usual mistake.
Dropped on the ground with no fallen hero in range, it is wasted. The icon avoids that.
It takes two housing spaces, so it replaces something else.

Ice Block Spell.role: Freezes your own troops, so they take far less damage for a few seconds.
use: Cast it on big troops such as Golems, Lava Hounds or Yetis, once they draw fire deep in the base.
Follow with your damage troops while defences are wasting shots.
beware: Frozen troops cannot attack, so a badly timed one costs you damage.
It only catches units inside as it lands. Siege Machines are immune, and units from a dying Golem are not covered.

Totem Spell.role: Drops a tough totem that stuns defences on landing and takes their fire.
use: Drop it closer to the defence than your troops are. Defences retarget on the stun and can stay on nearer troops.
Use it to protect the unit carrying your funnel, or to soak a round of fire as the army moves up.
beware: Stun is brief and its health falls by itself, so timing matters. It deals no damage and sets off no traps.
Splash and multi-target defences still hit troops nearby. Monoliths and single-target Infernos melt it, so Freeze those instead.
Clone, Recall, Ice Block, Healers, Druids and support auras all skip it, so do not plan on boosting it.

Angry Spell.role: Makes troops inside it drop their target and go for the closest defence, for a short time.
use: Cast it on troops stuck on outside buildings, to turn them on the defences.
Cast it when the closest defence is the one you want, as they retarget at once.
It can steer a Dragon Duke opener at key defences, with Invisibility Spells removing targets you do not want.

use.t: With a Ruin Witch army, cast it on your attackers, not her. Buildings fall faster, so Knights arrive sooner.

beware: They go for the closest defence whichever it is, so check what is nearest before casting.
It adds no damage, and Siege Machines ignore it.
Troops entering during its first few seconds are caught too, so a later wave can get pulled in.

use: Queen Walk or Charge with Healers behind her is the classic plan.
Action Figure is the top pick by most guides. It summons a Giant Giant to tank and hides her for a second.

use.t: Giant Arrow kills Air Defenses and Air Sweepers from level 9 up, with double damage on Air Defenses. Bring it for air attacks.

beware.t: Low health. Use Invisibility or Freeze as an Inferno starts to burn her.

beware: Poison enemy Valkyries first, or she wastes her ability and Healers on them.

use: Walk with the main group: on foot for ground armies, flying for air armies.
In a Warden Walk he goes first, so his Tome will not cover the army behind him.
Eternal Tome is the safest first upgrade, as it protects the army through the worst moment.
Fireball hits the closest defence, so position him first. Rage Gem adds damage to troops around him.
beware: Low health. If he falls early, the army loses its protection.
Save the Tome for the core or a known blast. It fires by itself if he is about to fall, unless you change settings.

use: Drop her where she can jump to the first defence straight away.
Electro Boots is the top pick. Seeking Shield hits several defences on a charge, and Rocket Spear picks them off from long range.

use.t: Haste Vial is the usual partner for Electro Boots, for a fast charge.

use: She leads RC Walk and RC Charge plans, with Invisibility on the way in.
beware: Short range and alone, so she falls quickly if several defences lock on.
Skeleton Traps and enemy troops turn her aside. Electro Boots burn Skeletons off.

beware.t: Spirit Fox also makes Skeletons lose her.

use: In a Duke Charge he goes first. In Dragon armies he gives up his rage and tanks in front.
Otherwise send your ground push first, then drop him on a lane no friendly air unit will follow.
Fire Heart was the usual first pick, as Healers cannot heal him. October removed its damage, so test it. Flame Blower adds burst.
Rocket Backpack flies him through the base centre, so line up the angle. He cannot be targeted and sets off no traps.
beware: Friendly flyers near him switch off his rage. His own pet does not count, but Boogers and other heroes' flying pets do.
All traps hurt him more since July, and more again when his rage is off. Route around likely Seeking Air Mines.
He lands exposed after a Rocket Backpack, so have follow-up ready.

use.t: Fire his ability once he has lost health, as it heals him as well as raging him and calling Barbarians.

use: Send him along one side to take out a corner and start the funnel.

use.t: Spiky Ball is the usual first pick, and Earthquake Boots its usual partner. Giant Gauntlet with Rage Vial suits compartment pushes.
Time his ability by piece: Boots at a wall, Spiky Ball among buildings, Giant Gauntlet before heavy fire arrives.

beware: Melee, so walls and Clan Castle troops stall him.

beware.t: Earthquake Boots or Stick Horse get him past walls.
A single-target Inferno burns him quickly, so keep a Freeze back.

use: Drop him close to the defences you want cleared, not at the map edge.
He flies to the nearest buildings, so placement decides his route.
Dark Orb is the constant, as it slows and damages what it touches. Guides pair it with Dark Crown or Meteor Staff.
Fly him behind tougher air units, which take the fire while he shoots over them.
beware: He picks the nearest target of any kind, so nearby Clan Castle troops can distract him from what you sent him for.

beware.t: Keep him off an Electro Dragon lane, as clearing its path leaves chains fewer targets.

use: It jumps walls and runs ahead to tank, so send it with a fast hero such as the Royal Champion.
It hits targets close to its hero, so the defences she goes for fall sooner.
beware: It cannot hit air troops, and can run ahead of slow heroes and die alone.
Poor on ranged or flying heroes, as it fights close in.

use: Use it when your hero would otherwise stall at walls.
It suits a King going in close and can help a Queen, though it may pull her Healers towards itself.
beware: Ground only.
Its rage comes when the hero falls, which is late to be useful.

use: It hits its hero's target from a range set by that hero, so it suits the Warden and is poor on the King.

use.t: The usual Warden pick until Sneezy opens.
A good fit for the Minion Prince until Angry Jelly opens.
It hangs back behind the Dragon Duke, so defences rarely target it.

beware: Low health, so it needs its hero in front.

use: Best on long walks, as on a Queen Charge. It can heal flying heroes, but fast heroes leave it behind.
Slow heroes such as the King keep it in reach, so it fits there if the Queen does not need it.
beware: Steady healing does not save a hero from one big hit.

beware.t: Frosty often does more when the Queen fights inside the base behind tanks.

use: Pick it for heroes that dive alone into danger.
It starts as an egg, then hatches when the hero falls, giving them a few invulnerable seconds to finish a key target.
The Phoenix keeps fighting after the hero goes down.
beware: The hero falls again when the time ends, even unhurt, so do not plan on a second life.
It does nothing until that moment, so you give up steady value from another pet.

use: Its poison slows and hurts enemy heroes and troops, not buildings.
Bring it against Clan Castle troops that keep stalling your hero.
With no enemy units close by, it helps its hero attack buildings, which suits a ground mode Warden.
beware: Very fast, so it can arrive alone with slower heroes.
It does nothing to slow defences, so pick another pet when Infernos are the threat.

use: Strongest on the Royal Champion. She targets defences, so it stuns the very defences she is hitting.
It stuns defending heroes and Clan Castle troops too.

use.t: It gained new levels here in August 2026, so older ratings may undersell it.

beware: It dodges fire by burrowing, so it tanks less than a L.A.S.S.I.

use: Pick it when defences, not Clan Castle troops or traps, are what stop your hero.
Frostmites also help slow defences near the hero.
beware: Slowing is not stopping, so you still need a Freeze for Infernos.

use: It hides itself and its hero in repeated bursts, so defences and Skeletons must retarget.
Best on heroes that need to get deep, such as the Royal Champion and Dragon Duke.
beware: It fights close to its hero, so it runs ahead of long range heroes such as the Queen and Warden.
Poor on a King meant to tank, as going invisible passes the fire to your other troops.

use: Pick it when you want your hero on defences rather than chewing outside buildings.
A top pick for the Dragon Duke and Minion Prince.
beware: The effect lasts a set time after landing, so drop your hero close to the defences you want cleared.
It adds nothing on the Royal Champion, who already goes for defences.

use: Boogers attack buildings and take hits, so it suits an air mode Warden or the Minion Prince.
If its hero falls, it rages and goes for defences.
beware: Boogers near the Dragon Duke can cancel his rage.
It can expose the Queen to Air Defenses.

use: A farming pet. Its extra damage to resource buildings is what you pay for.
It goes for resource buildings near its hero, so drop that hero close to your loot targets.
beware: Swap it out before war, unless your plan needs storage damage.

Air Defense.role: Heavy single-target anti-air. It cannot touch ground troops at all.
use: Let Giants or a hero clear the outer ones, since they take no fire from it.

use.t: Remove one or two with Lightning plus Earthquake before an air attack. Count your spells first.
Send a Lava Hound first. It flies at Air Defenses and soaks up their shots.
Giant Arrow or Rocket Backpack can also take out a line of them before your air troops land.

beware: Small groups of Balloons. Send many at once, as it only hits one target per shot.

beware.t: A few big flyers. Healers, Dragons and flying heroes all take its full hit.

Air Sweeper.role: Does no damage. Blasts air troops back, leaving them longer under other defences.
use: Check its facing when scouting, then fly in from the side or behind.
Spread air troops in a wide arc, so one gust cannot push them all.
Ground troops or Lightning can remove it.

use.t: Rage or Haste gets pushed troops back quicker. Freeze stops the gusts.

beware: Slow flyers. Balloons lose the most time.

beware.t: Healers on a Queen Walk, which get blown away from her.
Electro Dragons lose time too, and Inferno Dragons lose their beam.

Archer Tower.role: Single-target tower that hits air and ground.
use: Swarm it. Each arrow kills one small troop, so a pack of Archers or Barbarians wins.
Give it a tank to shoot, so your damage troops survive.

use.t: Outside towers often fall to one strong troop, such as a Valkyrie or Super Barbarian.

beware: Lone troops and thin groups, which get picked off on the way in.

beware.t: Tanks walking up to a Fast Attack tower. It has less reach, but hits twice as fast.

meet.t: A finished base has 4 Archer Towers left, beside 2 Multi-Archer Towers.
A finished base has 2 Archer Towers left, beside 3 Multi-Archer Towers and a Multi-Gear Tower.

Bomb Tower.role: Short range ground splash that also explodes when destroyed.
use: Send a Giant or Golem in first, and hold melee troops back until it has gone.
It cannot hit air, so Balloons or Minions can remove one that your enemy's anti-air does not cover.

use.t: A Grand Warden can hit it from outside its reach.

beware: Melee troops that finish it off. Its death blast still goes off if it is frozen.
Skeletons and Witches, plus Hog Riders if Giant Bombs sit in a gap beside it.

Builder's Hut.role: Harmless early on. From TH14 it can carry a turret, and its Builder repairs nearby buildings.

use.t: Drop one Barbarian or Archer on a corner hut. Every building counts towards the 50% star.
Kill huts on your attack side, or catch them in your spells.
Freeze stops his repairs and Poison slows them. Lightning makes him drop his target.

beware.t: Nothing yet. A hut cannot shoot until it carries a turret.
Spell plans that leave a defence barely alive. He heals it back up, and your troops cannot hit him.
Your path. A turret hut counts as a defence, so Balloons and Hog Riders go for it.

Cannon.role: Basic single-target gun for ground troops. It can never hit air.
use: Swarm it with Barbarians or Archers, or let a Giant hold its fire.

use.t: Send Balloons or Minions if no anti-air covers it, as it cannot shoot back.

beware: Lone troops sent in one at a time, which it kills in turn.

beware.t: Wall Breakers, which it picks off before they reach the wall.
Giants, Hog Riders and Valkyries against Burst mode, though Burst wastes shots on swarms.

meet.t: A finished base has 3 Cannons left, beside 2 Ricochet Cannons.
A finished base has no plain Cannons. They have become Ricochet Cannons and part of the Multi-Gear Tower.

Eagle Artillery.role: Base-wide artillery for air and ground, up to TH16. At TH17 it merges into the Town Hall.
use: It sleeps until 200 housing is deployed. Spend that on your funnel first.
Heroes and spells count towards that, so a long hero walk can wake it early.
Freeze it just before a volley. Freezing in the long pause between volleys wastes the spell.
It can't hit closer than 7 tiles, so troops that reach it are safe from its shells.
beware: Tight clumps and heavy targets. Shells land where the most troop health is packed, often your King.
Slow attacks. Once awake it keeps firing volleys into your main army until destroyed.

Firespitter.role: Very long range flames that only fire inside a fixed cone, and shred big single targets.
use: Check its facing when scouting. Its cone is broad, so come from far to the side or behind.
A base has two, so the other may cover that angle. If you must cross, use Freeze or Overgrowth.
A Skeleton Spell in the cone gives it cheap targets to waste bursts on.
beware: Heroes and big troops, plus whatever stands behind them. Healers following a Queen get hit too.
Stacks of air and ground. Stray shots hit both, whichever one it aimed at.

Hidden Tesla.role: Stays hidden until something comes close, then zaps one target, air or ground.
use: Look for empty 2x2 gaps inside walls. These are often Teslas.
Set them off with one cheap troop, instead of walking your army in.
They are thin and short range, so a Giant with Archers kills them.
Any still hidden come up once about half the base has fallen, so expect them late.
beware: Clusters of gaps, where several Teslas sit together. They melt anything you keep feeding into range.
Hog Riders and Balloons turn towards a revealed Tesla, and can leave your planned path.

Inferno Tower.role: Two modes. Single-target burns hotter the longer it holds, multi-target melts several troops at once.
use: Check its mode when you scout. One big lens on top means single-target, several lenses mean multi-target.
Single-target: Freeze it as it heats up, which resets the beam, or keep it busy with a swarm.
Multi-target: its damage stays fixed, so Healing Spells, Healers and several tanks can outlast it.
beware: Single-target: one tank or hero left under a fully heated beam.
Multi-target: swarms and small troops, such as Skeletons and Bats.

Monolith.role: Slow single shots with bonus damage based on the target's maximum health. Built to kill big units.
use: Freeze or Overgrowth stops it. Save one for when your key hero or tank comes into range.
Give it cheap targets. Skeleton or Bat Spells soak up its slow shots.
Expect a few shots on the first hero to arrive, so do not send a hurt one.

use.t: A Totem Spell also draws its shots.

beware: Heroes, Golems, Super Witches and anything else with lots of maximum health.
It hits one target, so spreading out does not save a tank. Cheap targets do.

Mortar.role: Slow long range splash for ground troops. One shell can wipe out a clump.
use: Spread Archers, Barbarians and Goblins out. Never drop them in one spot.
Send Giants first, so shells land on something tough. Fast troops often outrun the shell.
It cannot hit air, or troops right beside it. So fly, or get close.
beware: Clumps of small ground troops, and slow groups that stay in its range.

beware.t: A geared-up Mortar fires shells in quick runs, so one clump can take several.

Multi-Archer Tower.role: Merged tower that fires three arrows at up to three targets, air or ground.
use: Do not send a hero in alone. Puppets or a group of small troops spread the arrows.
Swarms still work, as three arrows cannot keep up with a big pack.
Time a Freeze for when your main damage arrives. Air armies should remove it early.
beware: Lone targets. With one troop in range, all three arrows hit it.
Lava Pups, as the arrows spread on to them once a Lava Hound dies.

meet.t: A finished base has 2, made from 4 Archer Towers.
A finished base has 3, made from 6 Archer Towers.

Multi-Gear Tower.role: Merged tower with two modes. Both hit one target at a time, air or ground.
use: Long Range fires slowly at up to 12 tiles, so swarms of small troops waste its shots.
Fast Attack reaches only 8 tiles. Freeze it as tanks arrive, or hit it from further out.
It is thin for its level. Earthquake plus Lightning can remove it before the army arrives.
beware: Fast Attack: tanks and heroes that walk up to it unsupported.
Long Range: single big troops, which it starts hitting well before they get close.

meet.t: A finished base has 1, made from a geared up Archer Tower and a geared up Cannon.

Revenge Tower.role: Starts silent, then wakes and gets faster and deadlier as your attack destroys buildings.
use: It wakes when 5 buildings have fallen, speeds up at 25 and peaks at 50. Aim to kill it before 25.
Freeze stops it. Totem and Ice Block soak up its shots.
Overgrowth only pauses it, as it keeps counting fallen buildings while rooted.
beware: Slow, deep attacks. Late on it fires quickly, and shots bounce on to nearby troops.
Clean-up troops at the end of an attack, as bounces hit air and ground alike.

Ricochet Cannon.role: Merged ground-only cannon whose shot bounces on to a second ground troop nearby.
use: Go air. Balloons or Dragons can destroy it without it firing a shot at them.
Spread ground troops, as the bounce only reaches a short way.
Freeze it as tanks arrive, which stops both shots while damage troops close in.
beware: Tight ground pushes, above all damage troops right behind a tank.
A hero walking with a ground pet. An air pet gives the bounce nothing to hit.

meet.t: A finished base has 2, made from 4 Cannons.
A finished base has 3, made from 6 Cannons.

Scattershot.role: Heavy shots at one target, then fragments spray over the troops behind it. Hits air and ground.
use: Bring your tank in from a different angle, so the spray misses your main army.
Freeze or Overgrowth it as your pack comes into range.
